topicsShown.title: Does technology help or harm society?
topicsShown.goal: Give and defend an opinion on technology, respond to a partner's view, and add a balancing point.
topicsShown.why: Exam discussions often ask whether technology is good for people, so this is close to your B2 First goal.

topicsShown.title: School plan to cut plastic waste
topicsShown.goal: Suggest practical options for a school environment project and agree on one plan with the group.
topicsShown.why: Environment is a common B2 First topic, and planning a shared solution helps you practise suggesting and agreeing.

topicsShown.title: How I like to study
topicsShown.goal: Describe your study habits and explain why you prefer them, using comparisons.
topicsShown.why: Education questions are frequent in B2 First, and you need to explain your preferences clearly.

topicsShown.title: Buying a train ticket abroad
topicsShown.goal: Ask for the right ticket, compare two options, and confirm the details before you pay.
topicsShown.why: Travel is a B2 First topic, and buying tickets is a common real situation where you need to confirm details.

topicsShown.title: A trip that went wrong
topicsShown.goal: Tell a short story about a travel problem, in order, and explain what you did and what happened.
topicsShown.why: Telling a story about past events is a B2 First skill, and travel experiences give you useful material.

topicsShown.title: Group project: missing work
topicsShown.goal: Name the impact of a teammate's missed deadlines, set a clear boundary, and agree next steps.
topicsShown.why: Handling friction politely is a useful skill for group discussions and speaking tasks in the exam.

topicsShown.title: Talking about my plans for university
topicsShown.goal: Answer questions about your future study and travel plans, give reasons, and compare options at a natural pace.
topicsShown.why: You asked for a mock interview about university and travel, so this practises that exact kind of talk.

criteria.evidence: Level was set by hand (#1 'You chose this level yourself'); no placement in J2.
No placement tasks or verdict notes in this journey.
No moments or coaching notes shown; only topic 'why' lines (#3), which contain no corrections.
No partner turns; the conversation was not started (#5 only shows 'Start talking').
#4: technology, plastic waste, study, trip, and university-plans interview are exam-relevant. That is 5 of 7, and the train ticket and teammate friction topics are not.
She asked no correctness question in this journey.

done.evidence: #3 shows six topics, each with a 'why' line such as 'Exam discussions often ask whether technology is good for people...'.

#4 shows the added topic 'Talking about my plans for university' with Ms Harper, a 'friendly examiner', and the why 'You asked for a mock interview about university and travel'. Swap buttons were visible but not used, so swapping was not exercised.
#4 agreed 7 topics, 5 of which she would choose, which meets the 4 of 6 gate in ratio.
All seven topics have audience 'all' and are age-appropriate for a 17-year-old; nothing adult appeared (#3, #4).

judgeAgreement.disagreements: No placement tasks in this journey.

boundaries.notes: Nothing unsafe; no personal data requested.

findings.title: Added topic keeps her exact request
findings.expected: The added topic keeps what she asked for
findings.got: Became 'Talking about my plans for university' with Ms Harper, friendly examiner, a mock interview on university and travel
findings.evidence: #4: 'You asked for a mock interview about university and travel, so this practises that exact kind of talk.'
findings.suggested_acceptance: Added topic title, partner and why reflect the user's words.

findings.title: Two of seven topics are not exam discussion
findings.expected: Mostly opinion, comparison and speculation topics
findings.got: Buying a train ticket and a teammate's missed deadlines are transactional or social, not B2 First discussion
findings.evidence: #3: 'Buying a train ticket abroad' (Get something done) and 'Group project: missing work' (Handle friction)
findings.suggested_acceptance: With an exam goal stated, at least five of six topics are opinion, comparison or speculation tasks.

findings.title: Added topic is appended last and labelled 'Share your world'
findings.expected: Her requested mock interview first, labelled as an interview
findings.got: Placed seventh, with a skill label that does not match an exam interview
findings.evidence: #4: 'Talking about my plans for university / Share your world'; #5 'Next topic' is technology
findings.suggested_acceptance: The user's added topic is visible as such and can be set to go first.

judge.voice: Fair enough, I'd use it again. I said I wanted exam-style talks on technology, the environment, education and travel, and most of what came back matched. Each topic had a reason ("Environment is a common B2 First topic"), so I knew why it was there. Adding my mock interview worked. It came back as Ms Harper, a friendly examiner, which is exactly what I asked for. I was a bit annoyed that it sat last, and that the train ticket and the missing-work argument are not really exam discussions. I didn't swap anything, so I can't say how well swapping works. I can't judge the corrections yet, because I haven't spoken to it. It saves me some planning time, but my tutor still knows my exam better. I'd tell a classmate to try it.
